record.paper_title: Opportunities and open questions in modern β decay
record.context_brief: Enhanced isospin breaking in axial radiative corrections
record.original_question: How should unexpectedly large enhanced isospin-breaking effects in order-alpha axial-current radiative corrections be computed, and can dedicated lattice-QCD plus finite-photon-mass lattice-QED calculations reduce the uncertainty in the renormalization of lambda = gA/gV used to compare lattice and experimental determinations of gA?

evidence.quote: Since then, a number of different works have appeared and while the contributions from the γW box are reasonably well understood, unexpectedly large changes were found due to enhanced isospin breaking effects within the O(α) calculation. This remains an open problem, and likely needs dedicated lattice QCD calculations, discussed below.
In order to resolve the uncertainty in Eq. (40) one may calculate its effect directly on the lattice.

This requires a number of non-trivial calculations, such as the finite volume corrections, the modification of the electron propagator in the QED background, and the non-perturbative renormalization of the calculation (118). In order to reach the required precision for a determination of Eq. (40), substantial computing power is likely required.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the axial-vector coupling $g_A$ and the vector coupling $g_V$ of the nucleon that govern neutron beta decay $n \to p e^- \bar\nu_e$, and define their ratio $\lambda = g_A/g_V$. At order $\alpha$ in the electroweak Standard Model, the radiative corrections to the axial current decompose into a $\gamma W$-box contribution (which is comparatively well controlled) and additional isospin-breaking contributions arising from the difference between up and down quark masses together with electromagnetism. Recent analyses indicate that these enhanced isospin-breaking pieces produce unexpectedly large shifts in the $O(\alpha)$ renormalization factor relating $\lambda$ as defined in pure QCD (and computed on the lattice) to $\lambda$ as extracted from experimental neutron beta-decay observables.

(a) Provide a controlled theoretical computation of the enhanced isospin-breaking contributions to the $O(\alpha)$ axial-current radiative corrections, identifying all hadronic structure-dependent pieces and quantifying their parametric and numerical size.

(b) Formulate a lattice-QCD plus lattice-QED calculation (e.g., using a finite photon mass as an infrared regulator) that directly computes the relevant $O(\alpha)$ isospin-breaking correction to the renormalization of $\lambda$. Specify and carry out the necessary ingredients: finite-volume corrections for QED in a finite box, the modification of the electron propagator in the QED background, and the non-perturbative renormalization of the relevant currents. Demonstrate that the resulting uncertainty on the renormalization factor relating lattice and experimental determinations of $\lambda = g_A/g_V$ can be reduced below the precision target needed for current neutron-decay phenomenology.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature confirms that lattice QCD+QED methodology for isospin-breaking and electromagnetic corrections is actively developing (e.g., RBC/UKQCD leptonic-decay work, C* boundary-condition QCD+QED, finite-volume QED schemes), but no published lattice-QCD+QED calculation has yet delivered the dedicated $O(\alpha)$ enhanced-isospin-breaking correction to the renormalization of $\lambda = g_A/g_V$ at the required precision. The issue of unexpectedly large enhanced isospin-breaking effects in axial radiative corrections remains an outstanding problem.

status_evidence.title: QED corrections to hadronic processes in lattice QCD
status_evidence.snippet: Framework for incorporating QED corrections into lattice QCD calculations of hadronic processes.
status_evidence.claim: Methodology exists for lattice QCD+QED computation of electromagnetic corrections, but specific application to axial-current renormalization for gA/gV is not yet realized.

status_evidence.title: First results on QCD+QED with C* boundary conditions
status_evidence.snippet: C* boundary conditions provide a gauge-invariant finite-volume formulation of QCD+QED for isospin-breaking and radiative corrections.
status_evidence.claim: Active development of QCD+QED lattice setups required to address such radiative corrections.

status_evidence.title: Isospin-breaking corrections to light-meson leptonic decays from lattice simulations at physical quark masses
status_evidence.snippet: Lattice computations of isospin-breaking corrections in leptonic decays at physical quark masses.
status_evidence.claim: Analogous techniques exist for mesonic processes; extension to nucleon axial radiative corrections is an ongoing program.
